memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: At Horeb you aroused the Lord's wrath so that he was angry enough to destroy you. When I went up on the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that the Lord had made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread and drank no water. The Lord gave me two stone tablets inscribed by the finger of God. On them were all the commandments the Lord proclaimed to you on the mountain out of the fire, on the day of the assembly. - Deut 9:8-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses recalls the terrible day at Horeb (Mount Sinai). While he was up on the mountain for forty days and nights — receiving the very tablets of the covenant, written by "the finger of God" — the people below were already turning away. God was giving them the words of the covenant even as they were breaking it. The tablets in Moses' hands and the rebellion in the camp form a heartbreaking contrast: God's faithfulness meeting human faithlessness in the very same moment.

It is worth pausing on how quickly it all unraveled. These were people who had seen the plagues, walked through the sea, and heard God's voice from the fire. Yet within weeks their hearts had wandered. It is a sobering reminder of how prone the human heart is to drift, even after the clearest experiences of God's power. We are never as far from spiritual danger as we like to think.

But notice also the beauty of the tablets "inscribed by the finger of God." God gave His people His word in permanent, holy form — a gift of grace even to a wandering people. And the fuller story of Scripture is that God did not give up when they broke His covenant. He would one day write His law not on stone but on human hearts, through His Spirit (Heb 8:10). Where we are prone to turn away so quickly, God remains faithful, and in Christ He gives us new hearts that can hold His word. Guard your heart from drifting, and lean on the God who keeps covenant even when we fail.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Am I aware of how quickly my own heart can drift from God?
- What recent experiences of God's goodness have I already begun to forget?
- How does God's faithfulness in the face of our failure encourage me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, my heart drifts so quickly, even after clear experiences of Your goodness. Thank You that You remain faithful when I fail, and that in Christ You give me a new heart. Guard me from wandering, and keep me close to You. Amen.
